transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me a little bit about what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in today because... I guess for a while now, I've been convinced that certain people—mostly in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati—are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. It sounds strange, I know, but I keep getting these little signals from them. It happens through things like event invitations, or the specific topics they choose for panels, or even just who ends up sitting near me at gatherings. Sometimes I try to tell myself it could just be a coincidence, but... I just can't really let it go. It's been bothering me a lot.
Have you ever heard any voices or sounds that other people around you couldn't hear?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or any sounds that aren't really there. It's really just the feeling of being watched and those signals I mentioned. That's what's been bothering me.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts about being tracked?
It's been going on for about two months now. Yeah, right around two months is when I first started noticing the signals and feeling like they were tracking my client meetings.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to organize your thoughts, or have you found it difficult to focus on your daily tasks since these concerns started?

No, not really. I... my thoughts feel pretty clear, actually. I haven't had any trouble organizing things or focusing on my daily tasks. I'm still able to do my job and get through my day just fine. It's really just those signals I mentioned that have been bothering me.
Do you ever feel that you have some special talent, power, or connection that might explain why these people are interested in tracking you?

No, I don't think I have any special powers or anything like that. I'm just a regular financial advisor trying to do my job. I don't know why they're interested in me, to be honest. It's just... I just know that they are. But there's nothing special about me that would explain it.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts were being controlled, broadcasted to others, or suddenly removed from your mind?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. My thoughts are my own, they just stay in my head. I don't feel like anyone is controlling them or taking them away... and I definitely don't think anyone else can hear them. It's just the tracking and the signals that I've been dealing with.

During these past two months, have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as feeling unusually depressed, hopeless, or conversely, feeling unusually energetic or needing much less sleep than usual?

No, my mood has been pretty normal, honestly. I haven't felt depressed or hopeless, and I'm definitely not bouncing off the walls with energy. My sleep is about the same as it always is. It's really just the stress from the tracking that's getting to me, but otherwise, I feel like myself.
Are you concerned that these people are trying to harm you, or do you feel they have some other specific motive for tracking your meetings?

I don't really know what their motive is. I don't... I haven't gotten the sense that they want to physically hurt me or anything like that. It's more just this constant surveillance. Like they need to know exactly who I'm talking to and what we're discussing during my client meetings. I don't know why they need that information, but I don't necessarily feel like my life is in danger. It's just very unsettling to know they're always watching.
How certain are you that these people are actually tracking your meetings, and is there any part of you that thinks it might be possible that you are misinterpreting these events?

I mean, I do try to tell myself that it could just be a coincidence. I really do try to look at it logically. But... I'm pretty convinced it's actually happening. 

It's specifically certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati. They are quietly tracking which clients I meet with, and then they send me these little signals. It happens through the specific invitations I get, or the panel topics they choose, or even who ends up sitting near me at events. So, even when I try to rationalize it and ask myself if I'm just misinterpreting things... I just can't really let it go. It feels too coordinated to be random.
Are there any other situations or people, outside of these specific circles in Cincinnati, that you feel are involved in this surveillance?

No, not really. I haven't noticed anything like this outside of those specific groups. 

It really just seems confined to the local arts and finance circles here in the city. When I'm talking to friends or, you know, family outside of work, or if I go out of town, I don't get that feeling at all. Everything feels perfectly normal in those situations. So, no, I don't think anyone else is involved. It's just tied to my work and those particular events.
